history.summary: 265-unit D14 leasehold (2022) at Mattar Road, DT25 at the doorstep, 2BR at $1.50M / $1,834psf. Good build (Keong Hong/Hock Lian Seng consortium, premium fittings) and frontier status, but URA appreciation is the weakest in the batch: 2.79% adjusted / just 1.73% resale-only, and asking PSF is far below the $2,076 median, signalling a soft submarket.
history.rating_rationale: A newish, well-built 2BR right at Mattar MRT in the Paya Lebar growth corridor is appealing, and the $1.50M quantum is accessible. But the resale-only URA CAGR of just 1.73%/yr is a genuine red flag — the lowest here — and the listing sits well under the $2,076 URA median, which points to weak transacted momentum rather than a bargain. Build quality and location are solid; the price trajectory is not. Net Neutral.

history.summary: A 2022, well-built (FSKH, premium fittings) D14 unit 470m from Mattar MRT, but at 883 sqft this is a very compact 'shoebox 3BR' at $1,812 psf. The decisive problem is appreciation: just 1.7%/yr resale-only (2.79% blended) over a thick 191-txn base — the weakest in the batch by far — signalling stalled price growth.
history.rating_rationale: Despite a strong location (470m to Mattar DTL, central D14, Paya Lebar Central catalyst) and good build quality, the investment math fails: URA resale-only appreciation is just 1.7%/yr over 191 transactions — a high-confidence read that this project has barely moved, well below the OCR/RCR baselines and the worst in the batch. The 883 sqft footprint for a 3BR is a compact/dual-key-style layout that squeezes liveability and narrows resale appeal. $1,812 psf with new-launch bias flagged means little discount and limited room to run. A modern build and decent transit cannot offset near-flat appreciation over a 5-7yr hold. Avoid.
